author: Alexandra Villarreal in New York
description:
Members of Congress seek to ‘bring sanity’ to system but decline to give details on plans to reform or abolish agency

A group of congressional Democrats on Wednesday pushed for immediate efforts to rein in the Trump administration’s sweeping immigration enforcement operation and “bring sanity” to an immigration system that Donald Trump said, after his party’s midterm drubbing, had been “too tough” in certain aspects.

Just over a week after the midterm elections in which the US president’s harsh crackdown on immigration fueled a voter backlash against Republicans, some sitting and newly elected Democrats gathered outside the US Capitol in Washington to advocate for a
title: Democrats push to rein in Trump on immigration after voter backlash to ICE raids

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
With year 12 exams under way, VCAA says there is no evidence any have leaked and hacker is attempting to exploit ‘anxious students’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority’s website has been hacked during the state’s exam period, with the culprit launching a tirade of expletives and claiming without evidence to have accessed student papers.

On Wednesday evening, a message attributed to someone using the alias “DaggerElite” appeared on the VCAA’s homepage banner, claiming to have sold exam papers to “hundreds of students” across the state.
title: Hacker claims to have sold VCE exam papers to hundreds of students after government website hack

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Group attending Veterans Day ceremony sharply reminded by sentinel to maintain ‘silence and respect’ at sacred site

A US army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier loudly reprimanded the embattled US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, and his top staffers on Wednesday, after some in the group were heard laughing and talking near the memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony.

According to video captured by the TV network pool, Hegseth was with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser and deputy assistant Tami Radabaugh walking up the steps in front of the memorial after posing for pictures. A laugh is audible, prompting the guard to yell: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” Hegseth looked over his shoulder in the direction of the soldier as he continued walking up the steps.
title: Hegseth and aides scolded by guard for laughing at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya and Damien Gayle in London
description:
Exclusive: Madeleine Alessandri, chair of the joint intelligence committee, will take on the role of advising No 10 on climate-related national security risks

The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.

Prime minister Andy Burnham will announce the move on Thursday at Cop31, the UN climate summit, with the new role designed to advise the government on national security risks from the climate crisis before they spell catastrophe.

Continue reading...
title: UK appoints world’s first special representative for climate security

author: Guardian staff
description:
Police called to Lane Cove North on Wednesday after sofa found containing human torso believed to be that of adult man

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

NSW police have launched a homicide investigation after a human torso was found in bushland on Sydney’s lower north shore.

Police said they were called to Lane Cove North about 2.30pm on Wednesday after receiving reports human remains had been found.

Continue reading...
title: Human torso found on sofa in Sydney bushland prompts homicide investigation

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Death of Javits Frimpong, who moved to the US from Ghana a year ago, has affected close-knit Ghanaian community

A 17-year-old boy has been arrested and charged with murder in connection with the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong in the Bronx.

The teenager was taken from his Bronx home for questioning Wednesday morning and brought to the New York City police department (NYPD)’s 42nd precinct. The suspect, whose identity has not been released, faces several charges, including murder, manslaughter, criminal possession of a weapon and other firearm-related offenses.

Continue reading...
title: 17-year-old charged in fatal Bronx shooting of 15-year-old boy

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Retailer’s management to seek two-week extension of legal protection from creditors in high court

MPs have accused the owner of Poundland of extracting millions of pounds from the retailer when it was on a “knife-edge” as the budget retailer seeks extra time to secure a rescue deal.

The management of Poundland, which employs 12,000 people and operates 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, will seek a two-week extension of legal protection from creditors from the high court on Thursday morning.

Continue reading...
title: Poundland owner extracted millions when chain was on ‘knife-edge’, MPs say

author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
description:
Paralympian Richard Whitehead ‘gobsmacked’ at Tory leader’s speech over proposed £36bn welfare cuts

The double amputee marathon runner Richard Whitehead has criticised Kemi Badenoch for “weaponising his sporting success” to justify her proposed £36bn welfare cuts.

In a speech this week, the Conservative party leader used the example of “double amputees running marathons” to explain the reasoning behind her proposed cuts to disability benefits, which she said were enabling people to “live a life of dependency”.

Continue reading...
title: Double amputee marathon runner criticises Badenoch for ‘weaponising his success’

author: Anna Betts
description:
Senah Park, 24, was last seen near Panther state beach on Sunday evening amid historic high tides and water levels

The US Coast Guard announced that it has suspended its search for a 24-year-old woman who is believed to have been swept out to sea in California.

The woman, identified as 24-year-old Senah Park, was last seen near Panther state beach in Santa Cruz county at about 8.30pm local time on Sunday, authorities said earlier this week.

Continue reading...
title: US Coast Guard suspends search for woman swept out to sea in California

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
PM wrote to transport commissioner to oppose ‘megashed’ in Astley shortly before he entered No 10

Andy Burnham raised safety concerns about dozens of lorries leaving a “monster” warehouse near a primary school because there was “no safe crossing” for children, a public inquiry has heard.

Concerns about the 18-metre-high “megashed” in the village of Astley, Greater Manchester, are being examined by Britain’s office of the transport commissioner.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham raised safety concerns about Manchester ‘monster’ warehouse, inquiry hears

author: Maya Yang
description:
Man, 30, is in custody in Florida and awaiting extradition to New York for alleged rapes at park in 2021, 2023 and this year

Authorities have arrested a man in Miami who is wanted in connection with three alleged rapes in New York’s Central Park, including one reported last month.

On Tuesday, authorities including the US Marshals took 30-year-old Dereck Rivera-Deleon into custody while he was working at a Burger King in Miami, New York City police said.

Continue reading...
title: Man arrested in Miami for three alleged rapes in New York’s Central Park

author: AFP
description:
Alexander Darchiev, who previously served as ambassador to Canada, died ‘suddenly’, said Russian foreign ministry

Russia’s ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, has died “suddenly” at the age of 66 after just one and a half years in the job, Moscow’s foreign ministry announced on Wednesday.

The ministry called Darchiev an “outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader and a kind colleague”. He was appointed to the position in March 2025.

Continue reading...
title: Russia’s ambassador to the United States dies, aged 66

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Equalities minister says Tories are ‘chasing Reform into the gutter’ as they drop support for planned law to ban ‘conversion therapy’

Kemi Badenoch has “no interest in supporting LGBT+ people” or promoting tolerance more widely, a government minister has said, after the Conservatives dropped support for a planned law to ban so-called “conversion therapy”.

The comments by Bridget Phillipson, the equalities minister, come after the Tories removed their previous backing for a law targeting abusive practices that aim to change someone’s sexual orientation or gender identity.

Continue reading...
title: Bridget Phillipson: Kemi Badenoch has ‘no interest in supporting LGBT+ people’

author: John Crace
description:
Even her own MPs were stony-faced as the Tory leader ran though her set list of gags from the budget to Russell Brand

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Well, there was one person at least who thought Kemi Badenoch had absolutely nailed it at this week’s prime minister’s questions. And that person was Kemi Badenoch. She could not have been more pleased with herself if she had tried. No one laughed louder and longer at her own jokes than she did. No one admired her laser focus as much as she did. Kemi is the paid up chief executive of her own fan club.

As for the rest of her Tory MPs – aside from Chris Philp, who is basically a parasitic homunculus – they weren’t quite so convinced by Kemi’s performance. She had been so entranced with her one-liners, she had forgotten to ask any serious questions. And
title: All Kemi had at PMQs was jokes … and unfunny jokes at that | John Crace

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
White House warns Democratic pledges to investigate president ‘may cross line into blatant criminality’

The incoming Democratic chair of the powerful congressional oversight committee said it appears Donald Trump has “something to hide” after the White House threatened criminal investigations over the party’s planned scrutiny of the administration.

Robert Garcia, ranking member of the oversight committee in the House of Representatives, vowed to press on in the face of what he

Continue reading...
title: Democrat says Trump has ‘something to hide’ after White House threatens oversight efforts

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
Ethics watchdogs question necessity of the US secretary of state flying between DC and Gainesville so often

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, has emerged as a superfan of the University of Florida’s football team, spending more than $1.2m of taxpayers’ money on frequent personal trips to watch them play, a report published Wednesday claims.

Ethics watchdogs have questioned the necessity of the country’s top diplomat shuttling so often between Washington DC and Gainesville, where his son Anthony has a walk-on role as a running back for the team known as the Gators.

Continue reading...
title: Marco Rubio spent over $1.2m of taxpayer money traveling to son’s football games

author: Achol Arok and Tara Conlan
description:
Children’s author and comedian, who wrote the book on which the movie Fing! is based, will also be removed from the publicity tour

  • Revealed: David Walliams accused of using celebrity status to prey on young women for sex

  • What are the key legal issues surrounding the David Walliams case?

The distributors of an upcoming Australian film based on a book by children’s author and television personality David Walliams have confirmed he will be removed from the film and its publicity run after sexual harassment allegations were made public.

Transmission Films has confirmed that Walliams, a co-writer of the children’s fantasy film Fing!, will no longer appear in the movie or take part in its media campai
title: David Walliams cameo cut from Australian film after sexual harassment allegations

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
PM welcomes cross-party push to reject ethnic basis for Englishness promoted by Reform UK politicians

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has said he is likely to support a bill tabled by a Liberal Democrat MP that would allow people to define themselves as both black and English for ethnicity options in the census for England.

The bill was drawn up by Josh Babarinde, the Lib Dem president, with backing from a cross-party mix of MPs including David Lammy, a former Labour deputy prime minister, and James Cleverly, the Conservative former foreign secretary.
title: Burnham signals support for bill to make ‘Black English’ and ‘Asian English’ census options

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Naresh Bhatt, 28, said he dismembered wife’s body after she took her own life, a claim prosecutors called ‘ridiculous’

A Virginia man who claimed he dismembered his wife’s body after she took her own life is facing a life sentence after a jury convicted him of first-degree murder.

Prosecutors in Manassas called it “ridiculous” that Naresh Bhatt insisted that he woke to find Mamta Kafle Bhatt, 28, dead from suicide in their bedroom in July 2024, then panicked because he thought he would be held responsible.

Continue reading...
title: Virginia man convicted of murder says he did not kill wife before dismembering her body

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Action on 25 and 26 November suspended to allow for formal negotations with the government

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Consultant doctors in England have decided to pause their two days of strike action at the end of the month.

Scheduled for 25 and 26 November, the action was announced by the British Medical Association when 18 months of talks with the government failed to lead to agreement on key issues.

Continue reading...
title: Consultant doctors in England call off two-day pay strike

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Prime minister tells Kemi Badenoch at PMQs that flagship strategy will be revealed before Commons Christmas recess

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The government’s 10-year plan will emerge by mid-December, Andy Burnham has told MPs, having previously raised the possibility it might be delayed until next year.

Quizzed by Kemi Badenoch at prime minister’s questions, Burnham told the Conservative leader the plan would be unveiled before the Commons Christmas recess, which begins on 17 December.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham says government will unveil 10-year plan by mid-December

author: Achol Arok
description:
While young people are drinking less across the board, one expert says a small minority are actually drinking huge and damaging amounts of alcohol

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Rising numbers of young people are being hospitalised with severe, irreversible liver disease, as alcohol-related hospital admissions remain above pre-pandemic levels after peaking during Covid lockdowns.

A new Burnet Institute report, commissioned by the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education (Fare), analysed nearly two decades of Victorian health data to examine the prevalence of alcohol-associated harm.
title: First Covid lockdowns, then alcohol to your door: rise in young Victorians with liver diseases prompts fears

author: Graham Readfearn in Antalya
description:
Australian PM boasts of success in renewables but is criticised for not addressing the nation’s huge coal industry

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese said governments had a “solemn responsibility” to act on climate change in a historic speech to the UN’s climate summit, but one which failed to mention the fossil fuels driving the crisis.

The Australia prime minister landed in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya on Wednesday morning where the Cop31 talks are being presided over by his climate change minister, Chris Bowen, but hosted by Turkey.

Continue reading...
title: Anthony Albanese fails to mention fossil fuels in Cop summit speech

author: Zoe Wood
description:
Pump prices stay stubbornly high as leading bank official warns energy costs are likely to remain ‘elevated’

  • Business live – latest updates

The price of diesel on UK forecourts remains stubbornly close to October’s record high of £2 despite a sharp fall in oil prices.

A litre costs an average of 197p, according to the AA, which described the situation as “dismal”. By contrast, petrol has fallen 6p to 168p from the peak of 174.7p in early October. That was the highest level since August 2022.
title: Diesel still costing close to a ’dismal’ £2 a litre despite oil price falls

author: Martin Belam
description:
House Republicans block impeachment resolution that cited US military actions in Iran, Yemen and Venezuela. Plus, SS United States to be sunk to create artificial reef

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. House Republicans have blocked an effort to impeach Pete Hegseth. The defense secretary dismissed the impeachment resolution from a Republican lawmaker as “political spectacle”, saying it was an attempt to set up a “show trial”. Top Democrats announced their support for the resolution, but Republicans moved to kill it by referring it to the judiciary committee.

Thomas Massie’s 34-page resolution, wh
title: Pete Hegseth survives effort to impeach him | First Thing

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas in New Orleans
description:
Richard Trahant says accusers have been vindicated after Catholic church officially classifies Paul Hart as sex abuser

An attorney who was fined more than $400,000 after getting an abusive Roman Catholic priest removed as a New Orleans high school’s chaplain says it was “worth it” now that the church has officially classified the cleric as a clergy molester.

That remark from Richard Trahant came days after the archdiocese of New Orleans, having waited years, added Paul Hart on 6 November to a list of Catholic priests and deacons faced with credible claims of clergy abuse while serving in the area.

Continue reading...
title: New Orleans attorney fined $400,000 after exposing abusive priest says it was ‘worth it’

author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
description:
Tactics to include GPS tagging for repeat offenders, high-street bans and tougher sentences

Five hundred of the most prolific shoplifters across England and Wales will be targeted in a police crackdown on retail crime, with tougher sentences, high-street bans and GPS tagging.

The home secretary said up to 17 police forces will target the repeat offenders in their area, collecting evidence of offences to secure stronger sentences and ensure they face “real consequences”, backed by an extra £2.5m in funding.

Continue reading...
title: Police to target 500 chronic shoplifters in retail crime crackdown in England and Wales

author: Eduardo Porter
description:
‘The post-election wish list is about to run into harsh fiscal reality: there is no money’

Is this an opportunity for a new America? As the Reagan revolution four decades ago launched US society down the path to low taxes and meager solidarity, perhaps the Republican bloodbath last week could turn US politics toward building a new social contract anchored on an aspiration to equitable prosperity.

One can sense the ambition of the bumper new crop of Democrats ushered to power last week, calling for support for programs for children and their parents; emphatically endorsing the long-held dream of Medicare for All. The project includes rolling back Donald Trump’s cuts to Medicaid and food stamps, and restoring subsidies for health insurance under the Affordable Care Act that Republicans allowed to expire. And that’s just the start.
title: Democrats’ US election sweep brings the price of their promised social contract into focus

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Package for plan off Norfolk coast revealed as government tries to calm critics after approving Jackdaw gasfield

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has hailed a record investment in offshore wind, as the government tries to repair its green credentials after approving the controversial Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea.

On Wednesday the government announced a £12bn investment from the German energy company RWE and the US private equity firm KKR, as the prime minister prepares to travel to the Cop31 climate crisis summit in Turkey.
title: Burnham lauds £12bn offshore wind investment as he prepares for climate summit

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Announcement comes ahead of visit to Cop31 climate conference with PM also set to face MPs at PMQs

The national security of all countries is at risk from the climate crisis, as “science fiction” scenarios of widespread destruction are already coming true and economic shocks from fossil fuels are now the norm rather than the exception, Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, will warn at the Cop31 summit today. Fiona Harvey has the story.

The CBI has issued a statement welcoming the PM’s offshore wind announcement. (See 8.55am.) This is from its chief executive, Rain Newton-Smith.

The prime minister’s announcement of major investment in offshore wind is a powerful restatement of the
title: Burnham hails approval for two huge windfarm projects as ‘power under British control’ – UK politics live

author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya
description:
Exclusive: UK foreign secretary to tell world leaders at Cop31 summit that sci-fi scenarios of destruction ‘now regular occurrences’

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The national security of all countries is at risk from the climate crisis, as “science fiction” scenarios of widespread destruction are already coming true and economic shocks from fossil fuels are now the norm rather than the exception, the UK’s foreign secretary is to warn world leaders gathered in Turkey on Wednesday.

Ed Miliband will tell the
title: Ed Miliband says national security of all countries at risk from climate crisis

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Share of CBA customers struggling to repay their mortgages has climbed to 12-year high

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

New lending to property investors fell at its fastest pace on record through the three months to September, as landlords adjust to higher taxes against a backdrop of plunging property prices and rising interest rates.

The latest figures come as the country’s biggest lender, the Commonwealth Bank, reported that the share of its customers struggling
title: Lending to property investors falls at record pace, as Australians fall behind on home loans

author: Richard Adams Education editor
description:
Office for Students says institutions in England should return to traditional exams and in-person presentations

Universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations to grade students after lecturers complained that AI has made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework, according to an investigation by England’s higher education regulator.

The Office for Students (OfS) said the credibility of degrees from England’s universities was under threat from the prolific use of AI in essays, dissertations and “open book” exams, with students reporting that their peers boasted of using AI undetected by staff.

Continue reading...
title: AI has made it ‘close to impossible’ to assess university coursework, regulator says

author: Henry Belot
description:
Exclusive: Chris Moore, running for the party in Greenvale, made derogatory social media comments between 2010 and 2012

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A One Nation candidate in Victoria has apologised for a series of offensive comments including repeated references to Australian-Indians as “curry munchers”, comparing a woman in burqa to a bag of rubbish, and sharing an image calling Julia Gillard a slut.

The party’s candidate for Greenvale on Melbourne’s north-western fringe, Chris Moore, also made derogatory comments about lesbians and refugees and once posted that he “doesn’t like the way the new homo cleaner at work looks at me”.
title: One Nation Victoria candidate apologises for slew of offensive comments about lesbians, Indians and Julia Gillard

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Supermarket’s move labelled ‘shortsighted’ by worker who calls upper management ‘woefully out of touch with reality’

Aldi’s UK business is cutting hundreds of head office and logistics roles as part of a global effort to trim costs at the budget grocer.

The retailer is consulting with its technology team on the loss of up to 150 roles after 103 redundancies in its finance and administration team earlier this year and almost 20 more redundancies among buying directors.

Continue reading...
title: Aldi cuts hundreds of UK head office and logistics roles as part of global cost trimming

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Antonia Romeo pledges to ‘rewire’ civil service by incentivising and rewarding top performers

Whitehall is too “tame, reactive and risk-averse”, the cabinet secretary has said, as she set out a “completely new approach” to managing the performance of civil servants.

With Andy Burnham and his deputy, Louise Haigh, in the audience, the UK’s most senior civil servant, Antonia Romeo, gave a lecture saying she would bring radical change to Whitehall as it deals with uncertainty caused by AI and global political tensions.

Continue reading...
title: Whitehall is too ‘tame, reactive and risk-averse’, says UK’s top civil servant

author: Kaamil Ahmed
description:
Charities warn of lack of protection amid health fears for more than 940,000 displaced people living in flood-prone areas

Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been left in waterlogged and damaged tents after deadly storms at the weekend, while 150,000 new shelters are held outside Gaza awaiting Israeli approval to enter, aid agencies have said.

At least four Palestinian children and woman were killed as heavy rains and wind battered fragile, leaky tents. Thousands have been left without shelter and sanitation infrastructure has been destroyed, with sewage spewing into people’s tents.
title: Thousands without shelter face lethal conditions in storm-hit Gaza as they wait for 150,000 tents

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Three directors were fined a combined $90,000 in federal court judgment and disqualified from managing a corporation for between five and 10 years

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three directors of a collapsed funeral fund that marketed insurance to Aboriginal families have been banned from managing corporations for at least five years and ordered to pay a combined $90,000 after being found to have breached their duties to clients.

On Wednesday, federal court justice Geoffrey Kennett ordered the former director of the insurance company Youpla Group, previously the Aboriginal Community Benefit Fund (ACBF), Jonathan Law, to pay the common
title: Youpla directors disqualified over collapsed funeral fund that targeted Aboriginal families

author: Jonathan Barrett and Luca Ittimani
description:
Australia’s oldest department store collapsed into voluntary administration last week after years of steep losses

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

David Jones is set to shutter half of its department store network, triggering mass job losses under a sweeping restructure, the appointed receivers said on Wednesday.

David Jones employs more than 6,000 staff across 38 stores.

Continue reading...
title: David Jones to close half its stores, triggering mass job losses in ‘urgent restructure’

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Three others critically injured and taken to hospitals as reports say car crashed into food stand in North Hollywood

At least three people are dead and three critically injured, after a car struck pedestrians on a Los Angeles corner during Tuesday rush hour, authorities said.

The fatal crash took place near a North Hollywood metro station.

Continue reading...
title: Three dead in Los Angeles after driver crashes into pedestrians, officials say

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Exclusive: Jillian Segal suggested ‘transferring’ powers in updated report released a fortnight ago but government sources note media regulator already exists

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Albanese government won’t follow a suggestion by the antisemitism envoy to scrap the ABC and SBS ombudsmen and replace them with an external oversight body.

In a list of updated priorities released last month, Segal proposed an “external independent ombudsman” to monitor ABC and SBS coverage of the war in Gaza and to ensure publicly funded broadcasters were “held accountable to their own
title: Labor won’t scrap ABC and SBS ombudsmen in favour of external body as suggested by antisemitism envoy

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Dave Grohl tells Sydney crowd Russell, whose death was announced this week, was a ‘big’ hero of his

  • Todd Russell, Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor, dies aged 54 due to illness

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A solemn moment has broken up an otherwise raucous Foo Fighters Australian concert as the band’s frontman made a lengthy on-stage tribute to Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell.

The US band are touring Australia for the 16th time in their 32-year history and Tuesday night’s Sydney show coincided with the news of Russell’s
title: Foo Fighters interrupt Sydney concert to pay tribute to Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
NSW premier Chris Minns warned council would be complicit in any ‘illegal activities that occur at these protests’

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Newcastle council – home to the world’s largest coal port – has banned a climate group from holding any events on its land after consulting the New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, who warned the council would be complicit in any “illegal activities that occur at these protests”.

On Tuesday night the council’s independent lord mayor, Gavin Morris, used his casting vote to ban any licensing of Rising Tide’s events, claiming in a mayoral minute that the group had “broken the trust and faith of the Newcastle community” by defying police directions during past protests.
title: Rising Tide banned from using council land for protests at world’s largest coal port in Newcastle

author: Nino Bucci and Jack Larkin
description:
Former CFMEU official Paul Tzimas tells inquiry he suffered fractured ankle and a colleague was left with major injuries and severe PTSD

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former union official has told a royal commission that underworld figure Mick Gatto attended a meeting that was called after the official and a colleague were seriously assaulted at a construction site.

Paul Tzimas is the first witness associated with the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union to appear before the royal commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure construction projects in Victoria.
title: Underworld figure Mick Gatto attended CFMEU meeting after construction site assaults, Big Build royal commission told

author: Abené Clayton
description:
Tech consultant convicted of second-degree murder in 2023 stabbing death of Cash App founder

Nima Momeni, the man convicted of murdering Cash App founder Bob Lee, has been sentenced to 16 years to life.

Momeni, 42, has been in San Francisco’s county jail since late April of 2023, after he was arrested in connection with the stabbing death of Lee, who had created the mobile payment service and was serving as the chief product officer of the cryptocurrency MobileCoin at the time of his death.

Continue reading...
title: Nima Momeni sentenced to 16 years to life in murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Asic says customers should not have to check every transaction to ensure they receive the correct interest

Macquarie Bank is set to pay a $14m court-imposed penalty after it admitted to breaking the Corporations Act with its “welcome rate” promotions.

The penalty comes amid a crackdown by Australian Securities and Investments Commission over complex savings conditions that risk short-changing consumers grappling with the cost of living.

Continue reading...
title: Macquarie Bank to pay $14m penalty after confusing ‘welcome rate’ promotion

author: Jeremy Barr
description:
Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit

Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. The president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit stems from the BBC’s splicing together of disparate comments he made before the 6 January US Capitol insurrection, as rendered in a Panorama documentary called Trump: A Second Chance.

“Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the Court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” the Trump-appointed Florida district court judge wrote. “It would be difficult for the Court to accept a different framing without completely negating the significance and fragility of political elections.”
title: Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed

author: Cecilia Nowell
description:
250ft arch risks ‘permanently diminishing’ memorials to ex-president and relatives at Arlington cemetery, lawsuit says

Nine members of the Kennedy family political dynasty have sued the Trump administration, asking a federal judge to block the president’s plan to build a towering, gilded arch they say would cast a shadow over their relatives’ graves in Arlington national cemetery.

The family’s complaint states that the 25oft triumphal arch, topped with a Lady Liberty-like winged figure, would “obstruct the clear sightline of the Kennedy Gravesites” and “fundamentally alter the experience of visiting” their family’s memorial at Arlington national cemetery. The project, they argued in a statement, risks “permanently diminishing these memorials”.
title: Kennedys sue to block Trump’s gilded arch, saying it would ‘cast shadow’ over JFK grave site

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former police officer accused of murdering Baird and Luke Davies cross-examined in NSW supreme court

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon has denied making a fake dating app account of Jesse Baird after their breakup, a court has heard.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon denies making fake Grindr account for Jesse Baird, double murder trial hears

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Head of major review into adult social care will say that governments have been ‘asleep at the wheel’ of vital system

Successive governments in England have been “asleep at the wheel” on social care, leaving the system to grow as a chaotic patchwork of local services with no clear vision, Louise Casey, the head of the social care commission, is to warn.

Lady Casey, who is preparing proposals for a big review of adult social care, will say the result is that in effect “no one is in charge” of a system that provides vital services for millions of vulnerable people.

Continue reading...
title: ‘No one is in charge’: social care system in England in chaos, Louise Casey to say
